text:
Alex Chen: hey team, first week — trying to get my dev env working. who owns terraform state and service-account provisioning for dev clusters? i followed the onboarding doc but `terraform apply` errors with 403
Maria Soto: welcome! for dev infra, infra ownership is split: Platform/infra owns the state buckets and SA creation. ping @Devon King for the bucket name. usually we ask Platform to run the initial apply for new users. :wave:
Devon King: hey alex — i can help. what's the exact error? 403 usually means your user hasn't been granted the `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on the state bucket or the service account wasn't created.
Alex Chen: thanks. error snippet: ```Error: Error applying plan:
google_storage_bucket_object.cover: Error 403: The caller does not have storage.objects.create access to the specified bucket.```
Devon King: yep that's the bucket perms. can you share your GCP email? i'll check bucket ACLs and either add a service account or give you temporary access.
Alex Chen: alex.chen@redwood-infer.com
Devon King: ok i'll open a ticket with infra and grant a short-lived role. FYI our process is: 1) new user requests via #new-hires (or on ticket), 2) platform infra does initial `terraform apply` with a bootstrap SA, 3) we create per-user SA + key if needed. we prefer Workload Identity but for quick dev we may issue a key.
Sarah Patel: quick note from People Ops: if you need access for a contractor vs full-time, tell us — approvals differ. also add your manager in the ticket for audit trail.
infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-4021 created by Devon King: "grant temporary storage access to alex.chen@redwood-infer.com" — assignee: platform-oncall — status: triaged
Alex Chen: awesome, thanks all. one small follow-up: who do i ping for cluster kubeconfig rotation when the token expires?
Devon King: that's also Platform. file a subtask on INFRA-4021 or DM me. rotation scripts live in `infra/scripts/kube-rotate.sh` — use the `make dev-kube` shortcut in the onboarding repo.
Maria Soto: adding to that: if you hit CI flakes after pushing, check the per-route rate limits in Console -> Routes -> your-service. sometimes new apps default to very low quotas.
Alex Chen: super helpful, will wait for the ticket update. thanks :pray:
Devon King: np — i'll post the bucket name and the window when i'll run the apply. if anyone else reading this is onboarding, feel free to reuse this thread.
